As a developer, it’s important to recognize when a level isn’t quite hitting the mark. When this happens, you have to decide whether to rework it or scrap it entirely. This was a decision I had to make during the development of Aphotic Descent as the team’s lead. One of the promises of this game was to deliver exploring a creepy abandoned lab so this level was featured in the Vertical Slice. However, during playtests, players often got lost due to a confusing layout and poor use of space, which made exploration frustrating and disorienting. This level was central to the game’s identity so it wasn’t something we were willing to let go of easily. I ended up leading an entire redesign of this level and it was a significant risk, but one worth taking. Here’s what I did: ✅ Focused on flow: [...] but one worth taking. Here’s what I did: ✅ Focused on flow: The rework centered around improving layout flow so players were naturally guided through the environment. ✅ Introduced a central hub: We designed a main hub with themed set pieces connected to it, allowing players to easily return to a familiar point. ✅ Added subtle gating: Using Metroidvania-style progression, we discreetly guided players with upgrades that opened new areas as they advanced. The result was a more controlled environment where the layout encouraged guided exploration. Before, players got lost. Now, they were immersed. This was only possible because we ran into the layout issue to begin with, which gave us a vantage point to assess why it didn’t work. results.title: MoviePass Faces Legal Action After Customers Complain – NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth
results.content:
Some of its remaining customers are fed up.

"It's frustrating," said Catherine Berry, a MoviePass subscriber. "I feel like I've been cheated."

Berry paid $90 for a yearlong MoviePass subscription. It originally let her watch one movie a day in select theaters. She says she loved it for about a month -- before available movies stopped showing up in the MoviePass phone app.

"I was lucky to get maybe one a month in," Berry said.
